KyoubeAI now keeps its own board key alive, so plugin updates and the agent working rules no longer stop after 30 days.

## What's in 1.12.1

**The board key renews itself.** The key `kyoube setup` stores lasts 30 days. Until now, nothing renewed it. When it expired, plugin updates, the agent working rules and user groups stopped without notice, while the app kept running. KyoubeAI now replaces the key a week before it expires: it gets a new key for the same person, checks it works, stores it, and revokes the old one an hour later. You'll see the new key, named `kyoube (renewed)`, under **Settings → API keys**.

**Doctor shows when the key expires.** The `board key` line in `kyoube doctor` shows the expiry date. It warns if renewal isn't working, and it fails with the fix if the key has already expired.

## Update

From 1.12, run `./update.sh`. It backs up first, and `./update.sh --rollback` returns to 1.12. There are no database migrations. After a rollback nothing renews the key, so check `kyoube doctor` within the month.

If your install was set up more than 30 days ago, its key may already have expired. Check `kyoube doctor` before you update. If the `plugins` line says `Agent token did not verify`, run `docker compose exec app kyoube setup` and approve the link it prints, as an instance admin, then update. Details are in [docs/operations.md](https://github.com/KyoubeAI/KyoubeAI/blob/main/docs/operations.md#the-board-key-expires), and the full list of changes is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/KyoubeAI/KyoubeAI/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
